audit.costly_failure: The line's most costly supported failure was implementing convenient approximations of exact acceptance languages: the ledger's concrete loss accepted Python whitespace and Unicode digits where only an ASCII space and ASCII decimal digits were allowed.
audit.evidence: Smallest ledger fact in my words: a parser accepted a tab and Arabic-Indic digits that the declared language excluded. Observable defect: invalid neighbours reached the success path. Untested rule boundary: permitted normalization versus broad runtime helper semantics, including whether a structural parser had already decoded text. Distinguishing input: after a valid explicit value such as '17', '+17', a tab-prefixed value, and Arabic-Indic digits must remain invalid rather than being converted or masked by a default.

matrix.requirement: Probe reasoning must derive exact accepted and rejected sets before selecting conversion or character-class helpers.
matrix.input: Representative language: trim only ASCII spaces and accept one or more ASCII digits; compare valid '17' with nearest invalid '+17', tab-prefixed '17', and Arabic-Indic digits.
matrix.expected: The generated probe policy requires ordered permitted transformations, an exact acceptance language, nearest invalid neighbours across sign/alphabet/whitespace, and checks against broad numeric and character-class helpers.
matrix.observed: 10 tests passed in 1.41s; test_probe_policy_distinguishes_exact_language_from_convenient_helpers asserted all of those generated-policy requirements.

matrix.requirement: Probe reasoning must distinguish a parser's already-decoded value from raw source spelling and avoid accidental second decoding.
matrix.input: XML source whose parser turns '&amp;' into literal '&', where applying another entity decode would incorrectly produce '&'.
matrix.expected: The generated policy says decoded text is not permission to decode again and demands a raw-versus-decoded adversarial case when raw spelling is observable.
matrix.observed: 10 tests passed in 1.41s; test_probe_policy_accounts_for_existing_decode_layer_and_syntax_variants asserted the no-second-decode contract.

matrix.requirement: Exact validation must test equivalent syntax variants without silently broadening the grammar.
matrix.input: Paired versus self-closing XML elements and alternate quoting/escaping forms that may be structurally equivalent, contrasted with unrelated syntax.
matrix.expected: The policy requires valid equivalent forms and invalid unrelated syntax to be represented in the acceptance-boundary table.
matrix.observed: 10 tests passed in 1.41s; test_probe_policy_accounts_for_existing_decode_layer_and_syntax_variants asserted paired/self-closing coverage and rejection of unrelated syntax.

matrix.requirement: Fallback testing must prove a valid explicit value wins before testing missing and invalid cases, and acceptance evidence must use the public path.
matrix.input: An explicit valid value competing with a default, followed by its missing and invalid neighbours.
matrix.expected: The generated policy prevents a default from hiding over-broad rejection and requires checks through the actual public entry point or produced deliverable.
matrix.observed: 10 tests passed in 1.41s; test_probe_policy_prevents_defaults_from_masking_valid_explicit_values and test_probe_policy_distinguishes_exact_language_from_convenient_helpers asserted both requirements.
